basic_info.description:
I'm a builder with range: a University of Chicago CS PhD who can take an idea from first principles to a deployed system, whether that's an LLM product, a medical AI pipeline, or a high throughput infrastructure stack. I'm deeply motivated by medicine and human health, using machine learning to make diagnostics more interpretable, patient outcomes better, and healthcare tools more reliable and accessible. I do research with agentic AI, engineering discipline, reproducible experiments, careful evaluation, and interpretability because I care about what's true, safe, and actually useful in the real world. I'm also a serial entrepreneur who ships, iterates, and turns ambiguity into products people genuinely use, not just prototypes. I'm equally comfortable in deep technical work (modeling, retrieval/memory, systems, data) and in the product layer where design, usability, and trust determine whether something matters. Outside of tech, I'm a multidisciplinary creative model, singer, actress, and artist and I bring taste, storytelling, and emotional intelligence into how I build and communicate. Ultimately, I'm trying to make the world better: I want to create technology that is scientifically grounded, ethically responsible, and meaningfully improves people's lives. I'm not interested in choosing one lane. I'm interested in combining rigor, imagination, and execution to build things that last.

If you liked my video at the top, you can find it here: https://youtu.be/SlssfnVdLlA

projects.title: Euchre
projects.description: A program including 4 cpp files to play the game of euchre. Card.cpp Pack.cpp Player.cpp Euchre.cpp Euchre (pronounced 'YOO-kur') is a trick-taking card game popular in Michigan. It is most commonly played by four people in two partnerships with a deck of 24 cards. Partnerships accumulate points for winning tricks, and the game continues until one side reaches the maximum number of points. Wrote a simulator for a game of Euchre with abstract data types, object-oriented programming, and polymorphism. • Write a simulator using C++ object-oriented programming for a game of Euchre can be played by either AI player or human player or both • Implement an AI computer-controlled player of euchre which can play this game automatically according to the rules I set • Implement human-controlled player which reads input from the human user
